title.narrative: Regional Upgrades of Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures for Trade Project

description.narrative: The project supports the improvement of Sanitary and Phytosanitary measures (SPS) in Mongolia in compliance with the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on the Application of SPS measures. The improvement in the SPS system is an essential prerequisite for Mongolia to increase agriculture and food trade and diversify its economy. The project addresses this issue through upgrading of laboratories and inspections facilities, strengthening inspection management systems, and aligning SPS controls and inspections with international standards.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved SPS measures in compliance with the World Trade Organization

Number of documents required for approval of import and export of agrifood goods reduced by 25% (2014 baseline: 12 for import and 11 for export) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The government established a working group to streamline its procedure and reduce number of documents required for approval of import and export of agrifood goods in Q4 2021. The Parliament approved the Law on Licenses and Permission 2022. Data Source: Customs General Administration of Mongolia Annual Report
General Authority for Veterinary Service
Export and Import Map report by Mongolian National Chamber of Commerce and Industry
World Health Organization Annual Statistics and Report
World Bank's World Development Indicators Actual value: N

Time required to process import and export of agrifood goods reduced by 20% (2014 baseline: 45 days for import and 44 days for export) Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: The project baseline data was collected from and based on the "Roadmap to Doing Business in Mongolia" report prepared by the MNCCI in 2014. The said report was produced on an ad-hoc basis and has not been updated annually. The MNCCI has prepared a similar report on the export products only in 2018. Achievement indicators were updated based on the 2018 report. Data Source: Customs General Administration of Mongolia Annual Report
General Authority for Veterinary Service
Export and Import Map report by Mongolian National Chamber of Commerce and Industry
World Health Organization Annual Statistics and Report
World Bank's World Development Indicators
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Laboratories and BCP inspection and quarantine facilities upgraded Indicator: 100 laboratory staff trained in SOP and 20 laboratory staff trained in in-depth testing methods (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The consulting firm has organized successfully all training under the Contract within 2021. The training series organized from September to December 2021 covered a total of 49 topics and involved approximately 4000 laboratory specialists (in duplicate counting) from both implementing agencies GASI and GAVS. At the request of the EA and IA, in-depth training for testing methods have been added and scheduled to be conducted within Q3 2026. Data Source: Training evaluation survey reports Actual value: Y

Output: Laboratories and BCP inspection and quarantine facilities upgraded Indicator: Five laboratories provided with new equipment to carry out diagnostic tests (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Procurement of the laboratory equipment is completed and handed over to the project IAs. 69 types of laboratory equipment, 43 types of reagents, 15,250 pieces of 19 types of portable inspection tools and 519 pieces of 19 types furniture was provided to the laboratories. The installation of equipment and furniture is completed in February 2025. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from contractors and annual project report Actual value: Y

Output: Laboratories and BCP inspection and quarantine facilities upgraded Indicator: Five new laboratory buildings constructed (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Civil works contractors to build 5 sanitary and phytosanitary laboratories is completed. The construction works of the Veterinary laboratory in Sainshand soum of Dornogovi aimag and Sanitary laboratory in Zamyn-Uud BCP are completed and commissioned in 2022-2023. The construction works of the Veterinary laboratory in Sukhbaatar soum of Selenge aimag and sanitary laboratory in Altanbulag BCP are completed and commissioned in Q4 2024. A number of new equipment was installed and relevant training on new equipment was conducted by the equipment supplier to those commissioned laboratories. The new laboratories started to function in a normal working regime. Remaining one laboratory building is completed and State Commission is scheduled to commence in February 2026. Darkhan laboratory is expected to be fully operational within March 2026. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from contractors and annual project report. Actual value: N

Output: Laboratories and BCP inspection and quarantine facilities upgraded Indicator: Portable laboratory equipment provided to 7 border crossing points (2015 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Based on the state expertise approved designs, it is clear that the project would experience cost overrun to construct proposed facilities. Thus, the EA has decided to scale down the size of the animal quarantine facilities to be built in Altanbulag BCP. A civil works contractor to build animal inspection/quarantine facility at Altanbulag BCP has started the construction work in June 2021. The progress rate is 5%. The works completed by the contractor was non-compliance with the quality against the approved DED. The conclusion was duly acknowledged by the employer and the contractor in December 2021. EA and ADB mission agreed to terminate the contract and to re-initiate the bid to complete construction at Altanbulag BCP soonest. New EA has established working group to process the contract termination agreement, and the termination agreement is signed. EA has requested to cancel the package due to limited time to construct the building before loan closing. During the Review Mission of 2025, the indicator has been revised. The procurement of the equipment is scheduled to commence in February 2026. The technical specifications are finalized by the IA. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from contractors and annual project report Actual value:

Output: SPS IMS established Indicator: Risk-based inspection system integrated into IMS (2014 baseline: no risk-based inspection system) Progress/Status: Completed. Equipment to complete the improvement of the inspection management system has been procured and handed over to the client. System commenced on 30 October 2025. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from information and communication technology firm Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SPS IMS established Indicator: SPS inspection management system improved (2014 baseline: no IMS) Progress/Status: Completed. The consultant has developed main modules of the SPS Inspection Management System, the SPS certificate issuance system and developed technical specifications of the IT equipment to support the SPS system operations. The development of risk management system is developed. The SPS IMS system is commenced on 30 October 2025. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports from information and communication technology firm Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SPS control and inspections aligned with international standards Indicator: International accreditation of laboratory tests (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Application for accreditation will be submitted when laboratories are constructed, and equipment installed. Data Source: Progress reports from Customs General Administration of Mongolia and General Authority for Veterinary Service Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: SPS control and inspections aligned with international standards Indicator: Laboratory manuals developed for testing and sampling techniques in line with international standards (2014 baseline: 0) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Laboratory manuals for testing and sampling techniques in line with the international standards have been developed. Under the contract CS9, the British Standard Institute, has developed SOP and operating manuals in line with ISO standard 17025:2005, and provided training to laboratory staff under 49 topics. Data Source: Progress reports from Customs General Administration of Mongolia and General Authority for Veterinary Service Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
